interactionPlan.concept: How backpropagation routes gradients through Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs), specifically showing how forward branches sum gradients in reverse.
elements: computation nodes (orange boxes, arranged in a custom DAG layout)
forward flow edges (black directed arrows pointing upwards)
backward flow edges (colored/highlighted directed arrows pointing downwards)
activation labels (values like x, h1, h2 flowing upwards)
gradient labels (values like dL/dx, dL/dh flowing downwards)
branch indicator annotation (highlighting the split at the bottom-right node)
merge indicator annotation (highlighting the join at the top-left node)

demo_steps.title: The Forward Pass & Branching
demo_steps.narration: In the forward pass, data flows from bottom to top. Notice the bottom-right node: its output branches (copies) to feed two separate paths.

demo_steps.title: The Forward Pass & Merging
demo_steps.narration: Further up, the left and middle paths merge into a single node. The inputs are concatenated or combined to compute the final output.

demo_steps.title: Backward Pass: Splitting at Merges
demo_steps.narration: Switching to backpropagation, gradients flow from top to bottom. At the forward merge point, the incoming gradient is split and routed back to its respective contributors.

demo_steps.title: Backward Pass: Summing at Branches
demo_steps.narration: Crucially, where the forward pass branched (copied), the backward pass must sum the incoming gradients. The bottom-right node receives and adds the gradients from both pathways.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A branching path in the forward pass (duplicating a variable) always becomes an additive junction in the backward pass (summing the incoming gradients).
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Arrange 7 orange square nodes in a 4-level DAG hierarchy. Level 1 (bottom): Node A (left), Node B (right, branches to two paths). Level 2: Node C (left, fed by A), Node D (middle, fed by B's left branch), Node E (right, fed by B's right branch). Level 3: Node F (middle, fed by D), Node G (right, fed by E). Level 4 (top): Node H (fed by C and F). Node H outputs to a top terminal arrow; Node G outputs directly to a second top terminal arrow. Forward arrows point upwards (black). When 'Backward Pass' is selected, display colored downward arrows showing gradient flow. When stepping through the slider, highlight the active nodes/edges in sequence (from bottom-to-top for Forward, and top-to-bottom for Backward) with dynamic label updates showing either activations (e.g., x -> x, x) or gradients (e.g., g1 + g2 -> g_sum).
